claimBlocks.suggestedSection: Southern language teaching and public cultural work
claimBlocks.text: The Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes describe teaching both distinct languages through community classes, youth outreach, Elder partnerships and an adult apprenticeship program. These are the institution's stated approaches, without a measured fluency outcome. Its Culture Program also describes representatives working on repatriation and with the National Park Service on public interpretation of Sand Creek. These responsibilities concern the shared Oklahoma institution, rather than every Arapaho community's programs or cultural authority.
claimBlocks.sourceLocator: Culture Program lines 7–11; Language Program lines 26–28

claimBlocks.suggestedSection: Finding the Oklahoma government's public institutions
claimBlocks.text: The Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes' government overview links its executive, legislative, judicial and Tribal Council branches. This provides an institutional starting point for the shared Oklahoma government; its organization should be kept distinct from Northern Arapaho institutions at Wind River.
claimBlocks.sourceLocator: Four branch descriptions, lines 8–36; final distinction is an editorial scope limit, with northern evidence supplied separately

claimBlocks.text: The Tribes' amended constitution identifies ratification on April 4, 2006. Its preamble links self-government with languages, education and protection of the natural environment. Article II establishes four branches, including the Tribal Council; Articles V–VI distinguish that adult membership body from a legislature representing four Cheyenne and four Arapaho districts. This describes the shared Oklahoma government's framework rather than a constitution for all Arapaho people.
claimBlocks.sourceLocator: Ratification PDF 2; preamble PDF 4; printed 4 Article II; printed 11 Article V section 1; printed 14 Article VI section 1

claimBlocks.text: In Latoya Lonelodge's 2023 Tribal Tribune interviews, Arapaho apprentice Arianna Long describes progressing from isolated words toward conversation and learning with coworkers while attending college. Rachelle RomanNose discusses pronunciation, expressing herself and the continuing work of learning. Her interest in teaching is an aspiration, not evidence that certification was completed. Their accounts bring individual Southern Arapaho women's voices into a discussion that also includes separately identified Cheyenne learners.

Replace or redistribute old p18-s1 paragraphs rather than append these blocks. Existing Language learning across generations and Cultural authority/repatriation paragraphs both cite it; their complete body, annotation, scope and any overview must be recomputed together. This packet's teaching/cultural claim is deliberately one 70-word block.

Government overview can remain a supporting source in a combined government section. If its claim is merged with the constitutional paragraph, charge the entire resulting paragraph to every cited work when checking derived-word limits. Do not retain an additional duplicate institutional paragraph automatically.

The amended constitution and official website program account are distinct authored works. The codes listing is an access route, not another substantive legal source. The Tribal Council and Legislative navigation pages are not additional source cards.

Cheyenne and Arapaho are distinct peoples within this shared Oklahoma government. Its constitution, programs and learners do not represent Northern Arapaho government, all Arapaho speakers or every Cheyenne community.

No current officeholder, population, certified-teacher total, classroom effectiveness, membership eligibility, legal advice, completed repatriation, ritual instruction, precise cultural site or source-media reuse is proposed. The bounded review is evidence for particular sections, not a declaration of profile completion.
researchGaps: Current program schedules, staffing, speaker totals, certification results and teaching outcomes require separate dated evidence; none follows from an undated program page or a 2023 interview.
The constitutional source is an officially linked amended compilation, not an independent determination that every current amendment or interpretation is represented.
Other Southern Arapaho community members' public accounts would broaden these institutional and two learner perspectives. Northern Arapaho and historical sources are outside this assigned packet.
No ceremonial applications, private family records, unpublished narratives or precise sensitive places were investigated.
